correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs finite Fourier positivity with counting normalization, derives the four-root minimum for all N>=5, and proves the odd contact equations have nonzero exact 6x6 determinants. The even contact nullspace is exactly three real edge-sum plus three imaginary vertex-potential dimensions; strict slack away from zero-sum Fourier contacts gives full relative dimension six. The asymptotic follows from the exact expression. Symbolic determinant and finite Fourier checks replayed from bundled code; finite data are not substituted for proof.

The latter equalities require contact matrices and nullspace structure.

originality.rationale: The known four-root minimum, Weyl-symmetric transform, finite-group Fourier positivity, and the resulting scalar mass are expressly acknowledged as antecedents. The newly established full complex equality class has a parity-dependent dimension jump (0 versus 6), verified by invertible odd-order contact matrices and even-order gradient/nullspace equations. Search comparisons found no statement implying that classification. Uninspected specialized Cayley-graph theta treatments remain a bounded residual novelty risk.
residual_risks: A specialized pre-2017 Cayley-graph Lovász-theta or finite-root-system Fourier paper could contain an equivalent optimizer-face classification under different language.
The 1986 Myerson source was not accessible in full; only its classical small-root minimization is asserted and credited.
The scalar extremal mass is largely implied by well-known symmetry and four-root facts; originality is attributed specifically to complete complex equality rigidity.

value.rationale: A3 is a canonical rank-three root neighborhood and a natural finite positive-definite support. The complete optimizer geometry exhibits an exact parity rigidity transition and a six-dimensional nonradial face, while the odd finite-grid mass approaches its limiting value at quartic order. These features are not mere reparameterization of the known four-root minimum or of the analogous 2D A2 case.
